@kpd_wrangler Yes, I read the changelog, before upgrading and again after your reply. This is not solved and it is not my calibration. I found the cause today.

PR #812 ("refactor spectral frame handling", merged Oct 22) changes the default in LineList.__init__ from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. So in 2.5.0 the rest wavelengths are vacuum unless you say otherwise. My spectra are calibrated in air from arc lamps. The vacuum/air ratio at 6563 A is about 1.00028, which is exactly the offset I reported (about 83 km/s), in the same direction for every object.

The only trace of this in CHANGES.md is "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)". Nobody can guess from the word "refactor" that a default changed and that redshifts will move. There is no deprecation warning either.

"Works for me" is not a test. If your data is already in vacuum wavelengths, or it is radio, then of course you see no difference. That says nothing about air-calibrated optical data. m_okonkwo posted further down about what looks like the same offset on long-slit data, so it is not only me.

After being told it was my own calibration, I spent two days assuming my wavelength solution was broken and re-reduced the arc lamps for 40 spectra. For nothing, the calibration was fine. A thread should not be marked solved when nobody has reproduced or explained the problem.

Workaround, for anyone who lands here with air wavelengths: set the frame explicitly.

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

That fixes it for me on 2.5.0.

To the maintainers, three requests:

1. Please reopen this thread, or at least remove the solved mark, so people searching for a redshift offset after 2.5.0 can find it.
2. Add a line to the 2.5.0 section of CHANGES.md saying that the default wave_frame changed from 'air' to 'vacuum' and that this shifts fitted redshifts for air-calibrated data.
3. Emit a warning when wave_frame is not set, at least for a release or two. A silent change of about 83 km/s is easy to miss and can end up in a paper.

I can open an issue or a PR for the changelog line if that helps.
